_about: Firmer dates for the timeline entries BibleWorks marked uncertain. Each gives the best-supported date or range, a clear title, and what the date rests on. Negative years are BC.

WILDRNSS-3.title: Psalm 90, the prayer of Moses
WILDRNSS-3.dating: Its title, "A prayer of Moses, the man of God", places it in his lifetime; it is set here in the forty years in the wilderness (Num 14:33-34).

PROMLAND-13.title: Samson judges Israel (20 years)
PROMLAND-13.dating: Twenty years (Judg 15:20; 16:31), within the forty years of Philistine rule (Judg 13:1) that ended with Samuel's victory at Mizpah.

PROMLAND-14.title: Samuel judges Israel
PROMLAND-14.dating: From the victory at Mizpah, twenty years after the ark came to Kiriath-jearim (1 Sam 7:2-13), to his death in Saul's last years (1 Sam 25:1).

KINGS-4.title: Psalms of David
KINGS-4.dating: David's life, from his anointing by Samuel (1 Sam 16) to his death after forty years as king (1 Kgs 2:10-11).

KINGS-23.title: Obadiah prophesies against Edom
KINGS-23.dating: Set in the reign of Jehoram of Judah, when Edom revolted and Jerusalem was plundered (2 Kgs 8:20-22; 2 Chr 21:16-17). Many modern scholars instead link it with Edom's part in the fall of Jerusalem in 586 BC.

KINGS-36.title: Jonah, prophet under Jeroboam II
KINGS-36.dating: 2 Kgs 14:25 names Jonah son of Amittai as prophet in the reign of Jeroboam II of Israel (793-753 BC).

KINGS-38.title: Amos prophesies, two years before the earthquake
KINGS-38.dating: Amos 1:1: under Uzziah and Jeroboam II, "two years before the earthquake"; excavations at Hazor and elsewhere date that earthquake to about 760 BC.

ASSYR-11.title: Sennacherib invades Judah and besieges Jerusalem
ASSYR-11.dating: Sennacherib's third campaign, 701 BC, recorded in his own annals (the Taylor Prism) and in 2 Kgs 18:13-19:36 and Isa 36-37.

ASSYR-18.title: Nahum prophesies the fall of Nineveh
ASSYR-18.dating: After the sack of Thebes (No-Amon, Nah 3:8) in 663 BC and before Nineveh fell in 612 BC.

ASSYR-19.title: Manasseh taken to Babylon by the Assyrians
ASSYR-19.dating: 2 Chr 33:11. Most likely when Ashurbanipal put down the Babylonian revolt of 652-648 BC and called his vassals to account.

ASSYR-22.title: Scythian invasion of Western Asia
ASSYR-22.dating: Herodotus (Histories 1.103-106) tells of a Scythian domination of Asia in the generation before the fall of Nineveh.

ASSYR-26.title: Zephaniah prophesies
ASSYR-26.dating: Zeph 1:1: in the days of Josiah (640-609 BC); the idolatry he condemns points to the years before Josiah's reform of 622 BC.

ASSYR-27.title: Habakkuk prophesies
ASSYR-27.dating: The Chaldeans are about to rise (Hab 1:6): just before or at Nebuchadnezzar's victory at Carchemish in 605 BC.

BABYLON-3.title: Nineveh falls to the Babylonians and Medes
BABYLON-3.dating: The Babylonian Chronicle dates the fall of Nineveh to Nabopolassar and the Medes in 612 BC; the last Assyrian king held out at Harran until 609 BC.

BABYLON-13.title: Zedekiah, last King of Judah
BABYLON-13.dating: Made king by Nebuchadnezzar in 597 BC (Babylonian Chronicle); eleven years (2 Kgs 24:18) to the fall of Jerusalem, dated 586 BC here (some reckon 587 BC).

BABYLON-19.title: Nabonidus, last King of Babylon
BABYLON-19.dating: From his accession in 556 BC to the fall of Babylon to Cyrus in October 539 BC (Nabonidus Chronicle).

PERSIAN-3.title: Joel prophesies
PERSIAN-3.dating: The book names no king; the Temple is standing (Joel 1:13-14) and no Assyrian or Babylonian threat appears, so most scholars place it after the Temple was rebuilt (515 BC). An older view put it in the 9th century BC.

PERSIAN-4.title: Cyrus becomes king of Anshan (Persia)
PERSIAN-4.dating: Cyrus II succeeded his father Cambyses I as king of Anshan in 559 BC.

PERSIAN-5.title: Cyrus defeats Astyages: Media and Persia united
PERSIAN-5.dating: The Nabonidus Chronicle records Astyages' army turning against him and Cyrus taking Ecbatana in 550 BC.

PERSIAN-19.title: Psalms of the return from exile (e.g. Pss 85, 126)
PERSIAN-19.dating: Psalms that celebrate the return (Ps 126:1, "When the Lord brought back the captivity of Sion"), from Cyrus's decree (538 BC) to Ezra's coming (458 BC).

PERSIAN-22.title: Malachi prophesies
PERSIAN-22.dating: The Temple is rebuilt and a Persian governor rules (Mal 1:8); the abuses he names are those Ezra and Nehemiah fought, so about 460-430 BC.

PERSIAN-27.title: Nehemiah's second term in Jerusalem
PERSIAN-27.dating: He went back to Artaxerxes in the king's 32nd year, 433/432 BC, and returned "after certain days" (Neh 13:6-7); how long he then governed is not recorded.

INTERTES-25.title: The Law translated into Greek at Alexandria (Septuagint)
INTERTES-25.dating: The Letter of Aristeas places the translation of the Law under Ptolemy II Philadelphus (285-246 BC); the rest of the Old Testament followed over the next century.

NT_DET-1.title: Jesus Christ
NT_DET-1.dating: Born before the death of Herod the Great in 4 BC (Matt 2:1, 19), most likely 6-5 BC; crucified under Pontius Pilate, most likely on Friday 7 April AD 30 (the alternative is 3 April AD 33).

NT_DET-6.title: "Forty-six years building this Temple" (John 2:20)
NT_DET-6.dating: Herod began rebuilding the Temple in his 18th year, 20/19 BC (Josephus, Antiquities 15.380); forty-six years later is the Passover of AD 28.

NT_DET-34.title: Paul's last journeys: Macedonia, Asia Minor, Crete and perhaps Spain
NT_DET-34.dating: After his release in Rome: Crete (Titus 1:5), Macedonia (1 Tim 1:3), Nicopolis (Titus 3:12). Spain was his plan (Rom 15:24, 28), and Clement of Rome says he reached "the limits of the West" (1 Clement 5).

NT_DET-40.title: Death of James the Just
NT_DET-40.dating: Josephus (Antiquities 20.200) says the high priest Ananus had James stoned in the interval between the death of Festus and the arrival of Albinus, AD 62.

NT_DET-44.title: John writes the Apocalypse on Patmos
NT_DET-44.dating: St Irenaeus says the vision was seen "towards the end of Domitian's reign" (Against Heresies 5.30.3), AD 95-96. Some date it to about AD 68, after Nero.
